obligations.name: AI literacy of the staff who operate or use it
obligations.evidence: Training plan per system and role; measures taken, not a guaranteed level (wording of Reg. 2026/1744)

obligations.name: Stop the prohibited use
obligations.evidence: Decision to stop, date, data deleted, supplier told

obligations.name: People told they are talking to an AI: the supplier's duty, checked by the employer
obligations.evidence: Screenshot of the notice; clause in the supplier contract

obligations.name: Use as instructed, with named human oversight
obligations.evidence: Instructions for use on file; named overseers with training and authority to override

obligations.name: Input data relevant and representative
obligations.evidence: Data checks before each run; who owns the input

obligations.name: Monitor; report risks and serious incidents; suspend
obligations.evidence: Monitoring routine; incident procedure with the supplier's contact

obligations.name: Keep the logs for at least six months
obligations.evidence: Retention setting; who can read the logs

obligations.name: Tell workers' representatives and affected workers before use
obligations.evidence: Dated notice to representatives and workers, through the national procedure

obligations.name: Data protection impact assessment built on the provider's information
obligations.evidence: DPIA signed off by the DPO; provider's Article 13 information attached

obligations.name: Tell the people decisions are made about
obligations.evidence: Notice in the candidate or employee journey

obligations.name: Explain a decision on request
obligations.evidence: Explanation template; who answers and how fast

obligations.name: Provider duties for a system built in-house
obligations.evidence: Quality management, technical documentation, conformity assessment, EU registration

obligations.name: Not-high-risk assessment documented
obligations.evidence: The provider's documented assessment, on file

obligations.name: Fundamental rights impact assessment before first use, results notified
obligations.evidence: The six elements of Art. 27(1), cross-referenced to the DPIA (Art. 27(4) as amended); notification to the market surveillance authority with the AI Office template (Art. 27(3), (5))

obligations.name: Register the use in the EU database; do not use an unregistered system
obligations.evidence: Registration record of the use; check that the provider registered the system (Art. 49(1))

worker_rules.name: Information on fully automated decision or monitoring systems
worker_rules.what: In writing, to each worker and to the union representatives (RSA/RSU): the aspects of the job affected, purposes, logic and functioning, data and main parameters, control and correction measures, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, possible discriminatory effects; in a structured, machine-readable format
worker_rules.timing: Before work starts; at least 24 hours before any change to that information

worker_rules.name: Agreement or authorisation for tools that allow remote monitoring
worker_rules.what: Only for organisational and production needs, safety or protection of company assets, and with an agreement with the union representatives or, failing that, authorisation by the labour inspectorate; tools used to do the work and attendance records are exempt; the data can be used only with adequate information to workers
worker_rules.timing: Before the tool is installed

worker_rules.name: Information and consultation on planned AI in work procedures
worker_rules.what: Inform the works council with the documents, and consult it while its views can still change the plan
worker_rules.timing: At the planning stage

worker_rules.name: Co-determination on technical devices able to monitor conduct or performance
worker_rules.what: A works agreement; without it the system cannot lawfully be used. Courts read 'able to' broadly, so systems that log identifiable use may also need one
worker_rules.timing: Before introduction

worker_rules.name: Co-determination on selection guidelines
worker_rules.source: BetrVG §95(1); (2a) where AI helps draw them up
worker_rules.what: Works council consent to the selection criteria the system applies
worker_rules.timing: Before use in hiring, transfer or dismissal decisions

worker_rules.name: An expert for the works council, deemed necessary for AI
worker_rules.what: An expert, agreed with the employer as to person, subject and cost; for AI its necessity is presumed
worker_rules.timing: When the works council assesses the system

worker_rules.name: Information on the parameters of algorithms affecting work
worker_rules.what: The parameters, rules and instructions the system is based on, to the works council
worker_rules.timing: With the periodicity that applies; before use is the prudent reading

worker_rules.name: Notice of monitoring other than video
worker_rules.what: Allowed only where needed for full use of working time and proper use of work tools; purpose, scope and method in the workplace rules
worker_rules.timing: At least two weeks before it starts; new hires in writing before they start

worker_rules.name: Information and consultation of the social and economic committee on AI in HR
worker_rules.source: Code du travail L2312-38 al. 1-2, L2312-8 II 4°, L2315-94 2°
worker_rules.what: In undertakings with at least 50 employees (L2312-1): inform the CSE before using methods or techniques that help recruit candidates and before introducing automated personnel management processing; consult it on the introduction of new technologies, with precise written information and enough time (L2312-15); it may appoint an expert
worker_rules.timing: Before use; consultation while the CSE's opinion can still be taken into account

worker_rules.name: Information and consultation before means of monitoring employees' activity
worker_rules.source: Code du travail L2312-38 al. 3, L2312-37 1°, L1121-1
worker_rules.what: Inform and consult the CSE before deciding to use means or techniques that allow employees' activity to be monitored; any restriction of rights must be justified by the task and proportionate to its aim
worker_rules.timing: Before the decision to implement

worker_rules.name: Tell each candidate and employee before the method is used on them
worker_rules.what: Candidates expressly told of the recruitment methods and techniques used on them, employees of the evaluation methods; no personal information collected by a device not brought to their knowledge first; methods relevant to their purpose; results confidential
worker_rules.timing: Before the method is used on the person

worker_rules.name: Works council advice on an important technological facility
worker_rules.what: In undertakings with at least 50 persons (art. 2): submit the proposed decision in writing with its reasons and expected consequences for staff; if the decision departs from the advice, wait a month before carrying it out
worker_rules.timing: Early enough for the advice to influence the decision materially

worker_rules.name: Works council consent on personal data, monitoring and staff assessment
worker_rules.what: Consent to the arrangement on processing and protecting staff personal data (k), on facilities able to observe or check attendance, behaviour or performance (l) and on staff assessment (g); a decision taken without consent or the cantonal court's permission is void if the works council invokes it in writing within a month
worker_rules.timing: Before the arrangement is adopted or changed

worker_rules.name: Works council consent on hiring, dismissal or promotion policy
worker_rules.what: Consent to an arrangement on hiring, dismissal or promotion policy, which the system's selection criteria put into practice; without it the decision can be declared void
worker_rules.timing: Before use in hiring or promotion

worker_rules.name: Information and consultation forum, where one has been set up
worker_rules.source: Employees (Provision of Information and Consultation) Act 2006, s. 4, 7, 10, Schedule 1 para. 3(c)
worker_rules.what: In undertakings with at least 50 employees that have an information and consultation arrangement (agreed, or the Standard Rules after a request by 10% of employees): information and consultation on decisions likely to lead to substantial changes in work organisation. Without one, Irish law adds no general duty; Art. 26(7) still applies to high-risk systems
worker_rules.timing: Under the arrangement; before the decision is the prudent reading

worker_rules.name: Tell the works council which employee data are processed automatically
worker_rules.what: Tell the works council what kinds of employee personal data are recorded automatically and which processing and transfers are planned; on request let it check their basis; discuss it in the joint consultations
worker_rules.timing: Before processing starts

worker_rules.name: Works council consent for personal data and assessment systems, replaceable by the conciliation board
worker_rules.what: Consent to systems that process employees' personal data beyond general personal details and qualifications, unless the use goes no further than duties under law, collective rules or the contract, and to systems for assessing employees; the conciliation board can replace a refused consent
worker_rules.timing: Before introduction: without consent the measure has no legal effect

worker_rules.name: Works council consent for control systems that touch human dignity, not replaceable
worker_rules.what: Consent to control measures and technical systems for monitoring employees that touch human dignity; no body can replace it, and a works agreement without a term can be ended at any time
worker_rules.timing: Before introduction: without consent the measure has no legal effect

worker_rules.name: Written information and consultation on a new technology with collective consequences
worker_rules.what: In undertakings with on average at least 50 workers, where at least 50% and 10 workers of the categories affected see their work change: written information on the technology, why it is introduced and its social consequences, and consultation of the works council or, failing that, the union delegation; failing that, dismissals linked to the technology are barred and cost three months' pay
worker_rules.timing: At the latest three months before implementation starts

worker_rules.name: Information before monitoring electronic online communications
worker_rules.what: Monitoring of network communication data only for the four purposes listed, stated explicitly; inform the works council (failing that the prevention committee, the union delegation or the workers) and each worker concerned of every aspect of the monitoring
worker_rules.timing: Before the monitoring system is installed

vendor_questions.question: Send the instructions for use, with every item Article 13(3) lists
vendor_questions.why: Using the system as instructed is the first deployer duty

vendor_questions.question: State the accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity levels the system was tested against, with the metrics, and the circumstances known to affect them
vendor_questions.why: Monitoring, the DPIA and the Italian and Spanish notices need them

vendor_questions.question: Give the system's performance for the groups of people it is used on
vendor_questions.why: The check for discriminatory effects starts here

vendor_questions.question: Describe the human oversight measures and the tools that help interpret the output
vendor_questions.why: The named overseers are trained on them

vendor_questions.question: Specify the input data the system expects, and the data it was trained, validated and tested on
vendor_questions.why: Input data must be relevant and representative

vendor_questions.question: Explain how we collect, store and read the logs, and confirm they can be kept at least six months
vendor_questions.why: Log retention is a deployer duty

vendor_questions.question: List the changes pre-determined at conformity assessment and commit to tell us before any significant design change
vendor_questions.why: A significant change ends the grace period of Art. 111(2)

vendor_questions.question: Name the contact and the procedure for reporting risks and serious incidents
vendor_questions.why: The employer must inform the provider without undue delay

vendor_questions.question: Provide the information we need for the data protection impact assessment
vendor_questions.why: The DPIA is built on the provider's information

vendor_questions.question: Explain what the system can show to explain an individual output
vendor_questions.why: The person concerned can ask for an explanation

vendor_questions.question: Confirm the conformity assessment, the EU declaration of conformity, the CE marking and the registration in the EU database
vendor_questions.why: A public employer may not use an unregistered system (Art. 26(8))

vendor_questions.question: Send the documented assessment that the system is not high-risk, and its registration
vendor_questions.why: The employer keeps it on file and relies on it

vendor_questions.question: Confirm people are told they are dealing with an AI, and put it in the contract
vendor_questions.why: The duty is the provider's; the employer checks it

vendor_questions.question: Confirm the system does not infer emotions, and will not without telling us first
vendor_questions.why: Emotion recognition at work is prohibited

vendor_questions.question: Provide the logic, main parameters and data categories the national notices to workers require
vendor_questions.article: IT D.lgs. 152/1997 art. 1-bis co. 2; ES ET art. 64.4.d; AT ArbVG §91(2)
vendor_questions.why: The employer writes the notices; the supplier holds the facts

vendor_questions.question: Provide training material for the people who will operate and use it

literacy.who: Everyone who operates or uses it
literacy.covers: What it does and does not do, its known limits, when not to rely on it, how to report a problem
Reading the output, automation bias, the authority to override or stop it, logs and incidents (Art. 14, 26(2))

literacy.who: Recruiters, managers and HR business partners who decide
literacy.covers: Telling the person (Art. 26(11)), explaining a decision on request (Art. 86), human review
Purpose and proportionality, what the data may and may not be used for, the national rules on telling workers

literacy.who: The owners of chatbots and assistants
literacy.covers: Saying it is an AI, handing over to a person, what it must not answer

literacy.who: The data and IT team that built it
literacy.covers: Provider duties (Art. 16), data governance, documentation, and why a retrained model is a significant change

literacy_evidence: Date, material and attendance for each module and person: the measures taken, not a level reached (Art. 4(1) as replaced by Reg. 2026/1744)

fria_elements.element: The deployer's processes in which the system is used, in line with its intended purpose
The period of time and the frequency of use
fria_elements.kit: To complete: not in the register

fria_elements.element: The categories of people and groups likely to be affected
fria_elements.kit: Register: applicants or employees, countries, department, workers in scope

fria_elements.element: The specific risks of harm to them, using the provider's Article 13 information
fria_elements.kit: Supplier answers V02-V03; the boundary cases in the report

fria_elements.element: How the human oversight measures of the instructions for use are put in place
fria_elements.kit: Obligation O04; supplier answer V04; literacy module L02

fria_elements.element: The measures if the risks materialise: internal governance and complaint mechanisms
fria_elements.kit: Obligations O06 and O11; supplier answer V08

not_applicable.name: Fundamental rights impact assessment for credit and insurance systems
not_applicable.why: Owed whatever the deployer for credit scoring and life and health insurance pricing; no HR system is one of them. For public bodies and public-service entities it is obligation O14.

not_applicable.name: Annex III point 3, education and vocational training
not_applicable.why: Covers education and vocational training institutions; an employer's course suggestions that do not feed promotion or pay are not in it.
